summary: David M. DiValerio specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the SIT Graduate Institute and earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer, holding a post at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee (attested 2015).

David M. Knipe is an Indology and religious studies scholar. He spent his career at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, serving as Professor and Chair of Religious Studies, and later as Professor Emeritus in the Department of Languages and Cultures of Asia.

David Matsumoto is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He served as Director at the Institute of Buddhist Studies (attested 2004, 2013) and is President Emeritus of the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research (attested 2026).

David N. Lorenzen is an Indologist and historian. Educated at Wesleyan, SOAS, and the Australian National University under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, he served as a professor and research scholar at El Colegio de México from 1970 to 2010 (emeritus 2019).

David Ownby is a historian and sinologist. After earning his B.A. from Vanderbilt and a Ph.D. from Harvard, he taught at Southern Methodist University (~1989–1993) and was Professor of History at the University of Montreal from 1994 to 2023.

David P. Jackson is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He earned his BA, MA, and PhD at the University of Washington, the latter under David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a C-3 professorship at the University of Hamburg from 1992 to 2007.
David Patt is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He earned his Doctor of Philosophy at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of Geshe Lhundub Sopa (attested 1993).

David Pingree was a scholar of Indology and history. He earned his bachelor's and doctorate from Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls and Otto Neugebauer. He held professorships at the University of Chicago (1963–1971) and Brown University (from 1971).

David R. Kinsley was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied at Drew University, Union Theological Seminary, and the University of Chicago, and spent his career at McMaster University from 1969 to 2000.

David R. Loy is a philosopher and Buddhist studies scholar. Educated at Carleton, Hawaiʻi, and the National University of Singapore, he taught at Singapore (1978–1984), Bunkyo University (1990–2006), and Xavier University (~2006–2010).

David Ralph Quinter is a scholar of Japanese religions and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA from the University of Colorado Boulder and a PhD from Stanford University under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, later joining the University of Alberta.

David Roy Shackleton Bailey was a scholar of Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Cambridge (Litt.D. 1958), he held appointments at Cambridge, Harvard University as Pope Professor of Latin (1975–1988), and the University of Michigan (1988–2002).

David Schaberg is a sinologist who studied at Stanford University and earned a PhD in Comparative Literature from Harvard University. Since 1996, he has been at the University of California, Los Angeles, where he became Dean of Humanities in 2012.

David Seyfort Ruegg was a Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology scholar. After studies at the EPHE and the University of Paris, he held chairs and professorships at Leiden (1966–1972), the University of Washington (1972–1984), Hamburg (1983–1990), and SOAS (~1989–2000).

David Shea was a scholar of Indology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Trinity College Dublin (1793) and served as Assistant Professor of Oriental Languages at the East India Company College until 1836.

David Snellgrove was a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Southampton and the University of Cambridge. He served as a professor at SOAS University of London and the University of London from 1950 to 1982.
David Steindl-Rast is a religious studies scholar who completed his studies at the University of Vienna and the Academy of Fine Arts Vienna between approximately 1945 and 1952.

David Tracy is a religious studies scholar and philosopher. Educated at St. Joseph's Seminary and the Pontifical Gregorian University, he lectured at the Catholic University of America (1967–1969) and was a professor at the University of Chicago from 1969 to 2006.

David W. Chappell was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. Educated at Mount Allison, McGill, and Yale (Ph.D.), he was a professor at the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa (~1972–2000) and taught at Soka University of America (~2000–2004).

David W. Tien is a sinologist and philosopher. He studied at McGill University, the University of Toronto, and the University of Michigan, where he earned his PhD under the supervision of James Robson (attested 2009).
